feedback.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x}={2}^{x+1}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x} & ={2}^{x+1} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({2}^{x+1})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =(x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡2+\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\end{aligned}
$$
